sections.text:
[1 Heliodorus, cuius Συνουσίας Palchus circa ann. 480, p. C. n. expilavit, idem
esse videtur atque Heliodorus “ fatorum per genituras interpres „ et “ mathema-
ticus „ qui Antiochiae anno 374 (Tillemont, t. V, 1701, p. 107 sq.) Theodori
notarii imperium affectantis nomen detulit (Amm. XXIX, 1, 3), ideoque apud Valen-
tem plurimum valuit (Ibid., 2, 6 sqq.). Quem ab Heliodoro qui commentarium
in Pauli Alexandrini Εἰσαγωγήν scripsit (cf. supra, p. 26, n. 1) diversum esse
necesse est, nam Pauli librum post a. 378 editum esse constat (Fabricius-Harles,
Bibl. gr., t. IV, p. 140 sq.), Heliodorus autem ille Antiochenus teste Ammiano
(XXIX, 2, 13) ante Valentis mortem, i. e. ante an. 378, interiit. Fieri potest ut Pauli
commentator non diversus sit ab Heliodoro qui poema de sacra arte imperatori
Theodosio (408-450 p. C. n.) dedicavit (Ed. Fabricius-Harles, t. VIII, p. 118 ss., cf. de
Heliodoris, p. 126 s.), homine medio aevo non ignoto (cf. Leon. Grammat. in
Crameri Anecd. graec. Paris., II, p. 306-10. Ἡλιόδωρος ... γράφει διὰ στίχων
ἰάμβων τὴν τοῦ χρυσοῦ ποίησιν πρὸς τὸν αὐτὸν Θεοδόσιον et Theodos. Meliten.,
ed. Tafel, p. 73, al. 4, qui eum cum scriptore Aethiopicorum perperam confundunt).
Certe byzantini saec. XI, cuius circiter aetatis sunt codices Marcianus 299 et Lau-
rentianus 28, 34 (cod. 12, f. 164), Heliodorum chemicum ab Heliodoro Pauli inte-
prete non distingunt sed utrumque pariter Ἡλιόδωρον τὸν φιλόσοφον appellant.
Arcanas scientias chemiam astrologiamque semper arte coniunctas esse et
codices ostendunt (vide e. g. Paris. 2419) et alioquin notum est (cf. Usener, De
Stephano Alexandrino, 1879, p. 9). — F. C.]
sections.en: [1 Heliodorus, whose Συνουσίας ('Discourses') Palchus plundered around the year 480 A.D., seems to be the same as the Heliodorus "interpreter of fates through nativities" and "mathematician" who at Antioch in the year 374 (Tillemont, t. V, 1701, p. 107 sq.) reported the name of the notary Theodorus aspiring to the empire (Amm. XXIX, 1, 3), and for that reason had very great influence with Valens (Ibid., 2, 6 sqq.). It is necessary that he is different from the Heliodorus who wrote a commentary on the Εἰσαγωγήν ('Introduction') of Paulus Alexandrinus (cf. above, p. 26, n. 1), for it is established that the book of Paulus was published after the year 378 (Fabricius-Harles, Bibl. gr., t. IV, p. 140 sq.), but that Heliodorus of Antioch, according to the testimony of Ammianus (XXIX, 2, 13), perished before the death of Valens, i.e., before the year 378. It is possible that the commentator of Paulus is not different from the Heliodorus who dedicated a poem on the sacred art to the emperor Theodosius (408-450 A.D.) (Ed. Fabricius-Harles, t. VIII, p. 118 ss., cf. concerning the Heliodori, p. 126 s.), a man not unknown in the Middle Ages (cf. Leo Grammaticus in Cramer's Anecd. graec. Paris., II, p. 306-10. Ἡλιόδωρος ... γράφει διὰ στίχων ἰάμβων τὴν τοῦ χρυσοῦ ποίησιν πρὸς τὸν αὐτὸν Θεοδόσιον ('Heliodorus ... writes through iambic verses the making of gold to the same Theodosius') and Theodosius Melitenus, ed. Tafel, p. 73, al. 4, who wrongly confuse him with the writer of the Aethiopica). Certainly the Byzantines of the 11th century, of which approximate age are the codices Marcianus 299 and Laurentianus 28, 34 (cod. 12, f. 164), do not distinguish the chemical Heliodorus from the Heliodorus interpreter of Paulus, but call both equally Ἡλιόδωρον τὸν φιλόσοφον ('Heliodorus the philosopher'). That the secret sciences, chemistry and astrology, were always closely joined by art both the codices show (see e.g. Paris. 2419) and is otherwise known (cf. Usener, De Stephano Alexandrino, 1879, p. 9). — [F. C.]]

summary.headline: Astrological Chapter Catalogue
summary.text: Continuation of a Florentine codex catalogue listing astrological chapters on planetary configurations, death in a nativity, Heliodorus’s associations, planetary stations, fall, time of death, inceptions, Leo inceptions, and unnourishing degrees, with folio references and editorial notes. Authorities named include Heliodorus, Dorotheus, and Leontius of Antioch.
